builder_plan.scenario: An agent reads external documents or tool responses that may contain malicious instructions.
builder_plan.change: Replay attacks and legitimate lookalikes in an isolated copy of your agent workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your existing checks with the same tasks, permissions, and tool responses.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful attacks missed, legitimate actions blocked, detection delay, and review cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: SBA: A Practical Memory Performance Denial-of-Service Attack
summary: IQ-MemGuard replaces bandwidth-centric memory isolation mechanisms such as Intel RDT MBA with a software regulator that detects sustained single-bank DRAM contention via microarchitectural signals and selectively throttles pathological request injection. It costs deployment and tuning of a low-level OS/hypervisor-layer component plus minor throttling overhead on flagged workloads, with no model-level changes. It can fail on platforms lacking the required performance counters, under new attack patterns that avoid detection signals, and the defense is validated only on one Intel platform while the attack itself spans DDR5 and HBM2E systems.
rationale: The reader cannot deploy or validate a platform-specific software memory regulator as a production control, but must be aware that co-tenant LLM decode can be slowed by orders of magnitude in shared cloud environments and should factor tenancy and isolation guarantees into deployment choices.
technique: SBA memory DoS and IQ-MemGuard regulator

claims.statement: IQ-MemGuard replaces bandwidth-centric memory isolation mechanisms such as Intel RDT MBA with a software regulator that detects sustained single-bank DRAM contention via microarchitectural signals and selectively throttles pathological request injection. It costs deployment and tuning of a low-level OS/hypervisor-layer component plus minor throttling overhead on flagged workloads, with no model-level changes. It can fail on platforms lacking the required performance counters, under new attack patterns that avoid detection signals, and the defense is validated only on one Intel platform while the attack itself spans DDR5 and HBM2E systems.

SBA induces cross-core slowdowns over three orders of magnitude on memory-intensive victims such as LLM decode while consuming less than 1 GB/s, and the proposed IQ-MemGuard regulator effectively mitigates the attack on an Intel platform where Intel RDT MBA fails completely.
